newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan construction shares up on sound '97 outlook.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan construction shares up on sound '97 outlook.

text.p: Shares of Taiwan's construction firms rose on Monday on expectations that most of them will see a high growth in their 1997 earnings, brokers said.

After 80 minutes, constructions were up 1.47 percent while the overall index had gained 0.68 percent. BES Engineering rose T$1.2 or 4.32 percent to T$29 and Pao Shiang rose by the daily seven percent limit to T$24.5.
"Most construction companies are forecast to enjoy an average of 20-30 percent growth in 1997 earnings," said Nikko Securities research chief Michael Hung.

Brokers said Taiwan's property market had started a gradual rebound in late 1996 after seven years of recession and that investors had begun putting money back into the market instead of holding it in banks.

"The annual interest rate for one-year time deposit is only six percent, but investing in the real estate market, you may gain some 30 percent in two years, or an annual return of 14 percent," Hung said.
